Let me think this through as the farmer.

---

Alright, this is what I'm looking at for this year. I'm 66, been working this ground for 40 years, so I know what it can do. With just me and my wife in the household, labor is the thing I have to watch most carefully — I can't do the heavy picking like I used to, and hiring hands is getting expensive.

Of my 9 mu, I keep 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my main income and our grain — and 3 mu in cotton on the western plot where the drainage is better. I've been doing it this way for about ten years. Cotton still pays better per mu than grain when prices hold, but the picking is brutal, so I keep it small.

**Wheat (6 mu):** I plant around October 10-12, depending on when the maize comes off and the soil moisture. I use a local improved variety, Jimai 22 usually — I buy fresh certified seed every two or three years and save between times. Base fertilizer goes in with the rotary tiller: about 40 kg of 18-18-18 compound per mu, which gives me roughly 7 kg N, 7 kg P₂O₅, 7 kg K₂O as base. Then I topdress 20 kg of urea per mu at jointing in mid-March, that's another 9 kg N — so call it 16 kg N total per mu. I know the book rate is maybe 14-15 kg N, but I've found that on my soil, which is a bit sandy, a little extra urea at jointing gives me more consistent heading. Irrigation: overwintering water in early December if it's been dry, then jointing, heading, and grain filling — usually 4 times because our well water is metered but not too expensive. Last year I got 480 kg/mu, so I'm targeting about the same.

**Maize (6 mu, after wheat):** Tight turnaround, I have to be on the planter within 3-4 days of combining the wheat. I direct-seed a Zhengdan 958-type hybrid into the stubble with my neighbor's pneumatic planter — 60 yuan/mu custom rate. Base compound at seeding (25 kg of 15-15-15), then a topdress of 18 kg urea at the large trumpet stage. That comes out to around 12 kg N per mu — summer maize doesn't need as much because the wheat residue mineralizes. I only irrigate once or twice depending on the July rains. Herbicide (atrazine + acetochlor) right after seeding is essential, and I usually spray once for corn borer around tasseling.

**Cotton (3 mu):** This is my problem crop at my age. I plant around April 20 under plastic mulch, variety is a Bt-type to cut down on bollworm sprays. Fertilizer: about 30 kg compound as base plus 12 kg urea at boll-setting, so maybe 13 kg N total. Even with Bt I still spray 3-4 times for aphids, mirids, and bollworm late in the season. Irrigation twice if we get a dry August. Picking is the killer — my wife and I do the first pick in mid-September, then I hire 2-3 women from the village for the main picks. Budget about 200-250 yuan/mu in hired labor alone.

Total input budget comes to around 7,000-7,500 yuan for the whole 9 mu. Cash on hand is tight in spring before the wheat harvest, so I usually buy cotton inputs on short credit from the agro-dealer and clear it in June.
